A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HUMOTO work. Their main text, tables, figures, equations, and appendices are readable and can be matched across layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset-quality measurements in Table 1, a 26-participant perceptual study in Section 4.2.2 and Figures 12–13, and simulation and model-evaluation examples in Section 5.

after.justification: v2 retains these original measurements, perceptual-study results, and simulation/model evaluations, and adds a qualitative pose-estimation example in Figure 9.

M1.justification: The scene-driven LLM scripting, Rokoko/dual-Kinect capture, FoundationPose tracking with dynamic resets, SAM2 masks, and artist cleaning pipeline remain unchanged. The scripting examples in Figure 14 are also retained.

E1.justification: The datasets and task coverage remain unchanged, including HUMOTO's 63 objects, 72 parts, and single performer. The additional Figure 9 example extends the existing occluded human-pose estimation demonstration without establishing a distinct task or domain.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains BEHAVE, OMOMO, IMHD, ParaHome, and Mixamo. The qualitative comparisons retain their existing methods, including MotionGPT, 4D Humans, TRAM, DexGraspNet, and Affordance Diffusion. NeuralDome was already listed in v1's Table 2; its new citation does not add a comparator.

E3.justification: The abstract and introduction revise the reported corpus size from 736 to 735 sequences. Figure 11 still reports 736, so this establishes a stated sample-count revision, not verified sequence removal or rerunning. The evaluation metrics and 26-participant study design remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 9 adds a counter-and-stools occlusion example with 4D Humans and TRAM predictions, extending the qualitative analysis of pose-estimation failures. The other case studies and appendix analyses are retained without new ablations or sensitivity tests.

E5.justification: The perceptual study retains the same participant count and mean/standard-deviation reporting, including Figure 12's SD labels. Neither version adds repeated-run information, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Figure 9 adds qualitative prediction results for the counter-and-stools example, and Table 2 removes its numerical hand-count column. Table 1's benchmark values and rankings and Figures 12–13's perceptual results are unchanged; no quantitative performance improvement is reported.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 retains the same metric definitions and Equations (1)–(8), including MSNR, penetration, contact entropy, and state consistency. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the detailed multi-object HOI dataset, scene-driven scripting and capture methodology, and quality metrics and benchmarks. The one-sequence count adjustment does not redefine these contributions or strengthen their scientific claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of motion quality, noise, contact accuracy, and downstream applicability are retained. Section 6 keeps the same limitations concerning a single performer's body and movement bias and the substantial manual cleaning effort.

D1.justification: Capture hardware, frame rate, synchronization, calibration, tracking and annotation details, appendix prompts, and the project-page address remain unchanged. The added acknowledgment of GPU support supplies no new experimental configuration or reproducibility instructions.

R1.justification: v2 adds the NeuralDome reference for the dataset already present in Table 2 and explicitly cites the existing FoundationPose reference in Section 3.2. The related-work discussion and novelty positioning otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: There are limited wording edits in Section 3.1, revised acknowledgments and funding information, and small label and cross-reference changes. The section sequence and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 2 moves from the appendix to the main text and loses its hand-count column; Table 1 loses its two Key Statistics columns. Figure 4 is refreshed, Figure 9 is expanded and recomposed, and the stray '-10' beneath Figure 8 disappears. Table 1's caption still describes the removed statistical columns.

improvement.justification: The additional Figure 9 example and citation fixes provide modest benefits. However, v2 introduces a 735-versus-736 sequence-count inconsistency between the abstract/introduction and Figure 11, leaves Table 1's caption describing removed columns, and drops Table 2's hand counts. These limited losses in consistency and detail outweigh the presentation gains, while the main scientific contribution and quantitative evidence remain unchanged.
